ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, a combined device of a long rod and two fixed pulleys is used to lift the heavy object M. One end of the long rod is placed on the ground and connected by a hinge to form a rotation axis; its endpoint is exactly at point 0 directly below the left pulley. A thin rope is tied at the midpoint C of the rod, passes over the two pulleys, and then has the heavy object M hung on it. The distance between point C and point o is L. Now a force is applied to the other end of the rod, causing it to rotate counterclockwise uniformly, slowly turning from the vertical position to the horizontal with angular velocity ω (turning through an angle of 90°). Which of the following statements about this process is correct? (　　)
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: The heavy object M undergoes variable-speed rectilinear motion

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, one end of the rod is at the ground hinge point O, and O is located directly below the left fixed pulley; point C on the rod is at a distance L from point O. The thin rope goes obliquely upward from point C around the left fixed pulley, then passes over the right fixed pulley, and finally hangs the heavy object M vertically downward. The segment of rope on the right side that suspends M is always vertical, and the rod, as shown in the figure, turns counterclockwise uniformly from the vertical position to the horizontal. Reasoning: Let the angle through which the rod has turned from the vertical position be θ=ωt, and let the fixed height of the left fixed pulley relative to O be h, that is, OP=h; the problem only states that it is directly above O, and does not require h=L. Point C moves in circular motion around O with radius L, so the rope length of the segment from C to the left fixed pulley can be written as a distance related to θ; for example, when ignoring the influence of the pulley radius, s(θ)=√(h²+L²-2hLcosθ). This quantity is not a linear function of θ, and differentiating with respect to time gives ds/dt=(hLωsinθ)/s(θ), whose magnitude changes with θ. The length of the entire rope remains unchanged, and the lengths of the horizontal rope segment between the two fixed pulleys and the portions around the pulleys remain unchanged, so the change in length of the vertical rope segment at the M end is opposite to the change in length of the segment from C to the left fixed pulley. Since the rope segment at the M end is always vertical, the heavy object M moves along a vertical straight line; and because the magnitude of its velocity changes with θ, the heavy object M undergoes variable-speed rectilinear motion.
